mainTopic: The rules of the inner sprinkling learned from the פסוק, and the dispute between רבי and רבי ישמעאל over how the יום הכפורים bull is included
overview: The גמרא finishes reading lessons out of the words of the פסוק about sprinkling blood inside the היכל. 'בדם' teaches that the bowl must hold enough blood for dipping from the start, and 'וטבל' teaches that the כהן must truly dip and not wipe the sides of the bowl. The גמרא shows why both words are needed. It then explains that the words 'מזבח קטרת סמים' teach that no blood may be sprinkled on the inner altar until it has been inaugurated with incense. Next comes a ברייתא that supports רב פפא: רבי learns from the extra word ״לַפָּר״ that the bull of יום הכפורים follows all these rules. רבי ישמעאל disagrees. He says a קל וחומר already teaches this, and he reads the two 'bulls' in the פסוק as the community's bull and the כהן משיח's bull. The גמרא then asks which unlike offerings his קל וחומר starts from. It rejects two guesses and settles on the communal-mistake bull and the goat of יום הכפורים. It begins to spell out his argument, which finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: Lessons from 'in the blood' and 'and he shall dip'
steps.stepSummary: The list of lessons from the פסוק ends. A wart on the finger is not a barrier. 'בדם' requires enough blood for dipping from the start. 'וטבל' means real dipping, not wiping.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...a wart on the finger is not a problem. 'In the blood' means the bowl must have enough blood to dip into from the very beginning. 'And he shall dip' means he must dip, and not wipe up blood from the sides of the bowl.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list of lessons it reads out of each word of the פסוק about how the כהן dips his finger and sprinkles the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first words close an earlier lesson: a wart on the finger does not count as a חציצה between the finger and the blood. Then two new rules come out of two words. 'בדם' sets how much blood must be in the bowl at the start. 'וטבל' sets how the כהן takes the blood each time: by dipping, never by wiping.

keyTerms.meaning: A wart or growth on the skin
Enough blood to dip a finger into
From the start
Wiping or soaking up leftover blood from the sides of the bowl

phrases.english: ...a wart that is on the finger.
phrases.notes: This sentence starts on the previous page. The point is that a wart on the finger does not count as a barrier between the finger and the blood.

phrases.english: 'In the blood': that there should be in the blood
a measure for dipping from the outset.
'And he shall dip': and not wipe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a list of lessons from the words of the פסוק that began on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bowl must hold enough blood for dipping from the start (בדם), and the כהן must dip, not wipe (וטבל).

steps.title: Why the Torah needed the word 'in the blood'
steps.stepSummary: If only 'וטבל' were written, we might think dipping is fine even if the bowl did not hold enough blood from the start. So the Torah wrote 'בדם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah had to write 'in the blood.' If it had written only 'and he shall dip,' I would have thought it is fine even when there was not enough blood for dipping at the start. So the Torah wrote 'in the blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why both words are needed. Here it shows what we would have gotten wrong without 'בדם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וטבל' alone only says each sprinkling needs a real dip. Without 'בדם' you might think the כהן could start with a little blood and add more before each dip. 'בדם' teaches that the full amount must be in the bowl from the beginning.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary (the opening of a צריכותא)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
I would have said (a mistaken first thought)

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write 'in the blood,'
for if the Merciful One had written only 'and he shall dip,'
I would have said: even though
there is not a measure for dipping from the outset;
phrases.notes: He means: it would be fine as long as more blood is added before each dip.

phrases.english: so the Merciful One wrote 'in the blood.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question of why both words from step 1 are needed, starting with 'בדם'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without 'בדם' we would allow starting with too little blood and refilling; 'בדם' requires a full amount from the start.

steps.title: Why the Torah needed the word 'and he shall dip'
steps.stepSummary: If only 'בדם' were written, we might think wiping blood from the bowl is fine. So the Torah wrote 'וטבל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Torah had written only 'in the blood,' I would have thought that even wiping is fine. So the Torah wrote 'and he shall dip.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of the צריכותא. It shows what we would have gotten wrong without 'וטבל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בדם' alone only makes sure there was enough blood at the start. As the blood runs low near the end, you might think the כהן could wipe the sides of the bowl. 'וטבל' teaches that every sprinkling needs a real dip, so there must be enough blood to dip into each time.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
Showing why each of two sources is needed

steps.whatToRemember: Both words are needed: 'בדם' requires a full amount from the start, and 'וטבל' requires a real dip each time, never wiping.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only 'in the blood,'
I would have said: even if he wipes;
phrases.notes: Picture the last sprinklings, when the blood is running low and he scrapes it from the sides.

phrases.english: so the Merciful One wrote 'and he shall dip.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 2 from the other side and completes the צריכותא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without 'וטבל' we would allow wiping; 'וטבל' requires a real dip each time.

steps.title: Why call it 'the altar of sweet incense'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק describes the inner altar as 'מזבח קטרת סמים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the words 'the altar of sweet incense'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another word in the same פסוק and asks what it adds. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already says the altar is 'לפני ה׳', which already tells us it is the inner altar. So calling it the altar of incense seems extra, and an extra phrase must be teaching something.

keyTerms.meaning: The altar of sweet incense, the inner golden altar
Why do I need it?

phrases.english: 'The altar of sweet incense': why do I need this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the dipping rules to another seemingly extra phrase in the same section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the description 'altar of sweet incense' teaches, since the altar is already identified.

steps.title: The altar must first be inaugurated with incense
steps.stepSummary: The phrase teaches that if the inner altar had not yet been inaugurated with incense, blood would not be sprinkled on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches that if the altar had not first been inaugurated with the incense, he would not sprinkle blood on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the phrase sets an order, so the altar has to be put into use with קטורת before blood may go on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words tie the altar's identity to the incense. Until the altar has had its חינוך through burning קטורת, it is not yet ready for the sprinkling of blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Was inaugurated, put into use for the first time
Sprinkles (blood)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the first use of the inner altar must be the קטורת, and only after that may blood be sprinkled on it.

phrases.english: That if the altar had not been inaugurated
with the sweet incense,
he would not sprinkle.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאִם לֹא נִתְחַנֵּךְ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ בִּקְטוֹרֶת הַסַּמִּים
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No blood may be sprinkled on the inner altar until it has been inaugurated with incense.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב פפא: the יום הכפורים bull is included
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא matches רב פפא's view. רבי learns from ״לַפָּר״ that the bull of יום הכפורים follows all the rules in the passage of the כהן משיח's bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רב פפא. The פסוק says 'And he shall do with the bull as he did.' Why does it add 'with the bull'? To include the bull of יום הכפורים in everything said in this passage. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב פפא's view. It says the extra word ״לַפָּר״ brings the יום הכפורים bull into the same blood rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three rules from the earlier steps were said about the bull of the כהן משיח: את (nothing may come between the finger and the blood, though a wart does not count), בדם (enough blood from the start) and וטבל (real dipping). The extra word ״לַפָּר״ stretches these rules to cover the bull of יום הכפורים too. That is exactly what רב פפא said.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him
Why does the פסוק need to say this?
To include
The bull the כהן גדול brings on יום הכפורים
In this passage

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא in agreement with רב פפא:
"And he shall do... as he did"
Why does the verse say "with the bull"?
To include the bull of יום הכפורים
in everything that is stated in this passage.
phrases.notes: These are the rules we just learned: את, בדם and וטבל.

phrases.english: These are the words of רבי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports, from a ברייתא, the view that the יום הכפורים bull shares the rules derived earlier.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's view that the יום הכפורים bull is included in the rules of את, בדם and וטבל
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי learns this from the extra word ״לַפָּר״ in ויקרא 4:20

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: a קל וחומר already teaches this
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל argues that no extra word is needed. If the Torah matches the blood actions of offerings that are not otherwise alike, it surely matches them where the offerings are alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said: this is a קל וחומר! In a case where one offering is not matched to another, the Torah still matched their actions. So in a case where the offerings are matched, isn't it logical that it would match their actions too?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל pushes back on רבי's way of learning. He says simple logic, a קל וחומר, already gives us this rule, so the extra word is not needed for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument runs from the weaker case to the stronger one. Some offerings are not alike, yet the Torah still gives them the same blood actions. The bull of the כהן משיח and the bull of יום הכפורים are alike, so they should certainly share the same actions. This leaves the word ״לַפָּר״ free to teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Logic from a lighter case to a stronger case
Was made equal or matched
Actions, here meaning the blood actions
Isn't it logical?

phrases.english: רבי ישמעאל said: this is a קל וחומר!

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁלֹּא הוּשְׁוָה קׇרְבָּן לְקׇרְבָּן –
phrases.english: Just as in a case where one offering was not matched to another offering,
the Torah still matched their actions to each other;
so in a case where it did match one offering to another,
isn't it logical that it should match action to action?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents רבי ישמעאל's disagreeing view within the same ברייתא: the יום הכפורים bull's rules come from a קל וחומר, not from the extra word ״לַפָּר״.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's use of ״לַפָּר״ to include the יום הכפורים bull
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule already follows from a קל וחומר, so the extra word cannot be needed for it.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's own reading of the two 'bulls'
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל reads the first 'bull' as the bull for a communal mistake and the second as the bull of the כהן משיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, why does the פסוק say 'with the bull'? That is the bull brought for a mistake of the community. 'With the bull' the second time means the bull of the כהן משיח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל has removed the need for the extra word. Now he explains what the two mentions of 'bull' in the פסוק really refer to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'he shall do with the bull as he did with the bull.' For רבי ישמעאל, it compares the community's bull (פר העלם דבר של צבור) to the bull of the כהן משיח. The two bulls follow the same rules, so the יום הכפורים bull is not mentioned here at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather
The bull brought when the community sinned by mistake because of a wrong court ruling
The bull brought by the anointed כהן גדול for his mistaken sin

phrases.english: Rather, why does the verse say "with the bull"?

phrases.aramaic: זֶה פַּר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִבּוּר.
phrases.english: This is the bull for a mistake of the community.
"With the bull" the second time is the bull of the anointed כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After freeing up the word, רבי ישמעאל gives it a new meaning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק compares the community's bull to the כהן משיח's bull, not to the יום הכפורים bull.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי learns the יום הכפורים bull from the extra word ״לַפָּר״. רבי ישמעאל learns it from a קל וחומר, and uses the word to compare the community's bull with the כהן משיח's bull.

steps.title: Which offerings were 'not matched' to each other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי ישמעאל's words and asks what case he meant by offerings that were not matched.
steps.simpleTranslation: The master said: 'Just as in a case where one offering was not matched to another.' What does 'one offering was not matched to another' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי ישמעאל's קל וחומר and asks a clarifying question. It is setting up the next move, which will explain which case he meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר needs a real starting case, so the גמרא wants to know where the Torah matched the actions of two offerings that are otherwise not alike. Without that case, the whole argument has nothing to stand on.

keyTerms.meaning: What?

phrases.english: The master said: "Just as in a case
where one offering was not matched to another offering."
What does "one offering was not matched to another" mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: וּמָה בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁלֹּא הוּשְׁוָה קׇרְבָּן לְקׇרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the קל וחומר of step 7 to clarify its starting case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which offerings are not alike yet still share the same blood actions, as the base of רבי ישמעאל's קל וחומר

steps.title: First guess: the bull and goat of יום הכפורים, rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the unmatched offerings are the bull and goat of יום הכפורים, but rejects this because their blood goes into the innermost chamber.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he meant the bull of יום הכפורים and the goat of יום הכפורים, this can be refuted: these two are special, because their blood is brought into the innermost chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first answer to the question from step 9 and immediately shows that it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the source case has no special feature that the target case lacks. The bull and goat of יום הכפורים have such a feature: their blood enters the innermost chamber, the קודש הקדשים. Because of that feature, they cannot serve as the starting point of רבי ישמעאל's argument.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (the opening of a suggestion that is about to be tested)
There is room to refute (the proof can be broken)
What about these? They have a special feature
The innermost chamber, the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: If you say: the bull of Yom Kippur
and the goat of Yom Kippur
this can be refuted:
What about these?
They are special, because their blood enters the innermost chamber!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא פַּר יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים וּשְׂעִיר יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים – אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to step 9's question and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects identifying the unmatched pair as the bull and goat of יום הכפורים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Their blood enters the קודש הקדשים, a special feature that breaks the קל וחומר.

steps.title: Second guess: the communal-mistake bull and the idolatry goats, rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the communal-mistake bull and the goats for communal idolatry, but rejects this because both atone for known sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Instead, say he meant the bull for a communal mistake and the goats for idolatry. This can also be refuted: these are special, because they atone for sins of a known commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second pair of offerings and again shows that the pair has a special feature, so it cannot be what רבי ישמעאל meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two offerings are also a bull and goats, so they look like a good example of 'unmatched' offerings. However, both of them come for a sin that is known to have been committed, while the bull of יום הכפורים atones for sins that are not known. That special feature lets someone refute the קל וחומר, so this pair fails as well.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull brought for a mistaken ruling that led the community to sin
The goats brought for a communal sin of idolatry done by mistake
A known commandment, meaning a sin people know was committed

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא פַּר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִבּוּר
phrases.english: Rather, the bull for a communal mistake
and the goats for idolatry
this can be refuted: What about these?
They are special, because they atone for transgressions
of a known commandment!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פַּר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִבּוּר וּשְׂעִירֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה – אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 10's guess failed, offers a second guess, which also fails.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects identifying the unmatched pair as the communal-mistake bull and the idolatry goats.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both atone for known sins, a special feature that breaks the קל וחומר.

steps.title: Final answer: the communal-mistake bull and the יום הכפורים goat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי ישמעאל meant the communal-mistake bull and the goat of יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant the bull for a communal mistake and the goat of יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: After two guesses failed, the גמרא gives its answer to the question from step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This pair mixes one offering from each of the failed guesses. Pairing these two avoids the problems raised in steps 10 and 11, since the גמרא raises no refutation against them.

keyTerms.meaning: The goat offered on יום הכפורים

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא פַּר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִבּוּר
phrases.english: Rather, the bull for a communal mistake
and the goat of Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פַּר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִבּוּר וְשָׂעִיר שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted answer after steps 10 and 11 were rejected.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which offerings רבי ישמעאל meant by 'offerings that were not matched'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The communal-mistake bull and the goat of יום הכפורים.

steps.title: Spelling out רבי ישמעאל's קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rebuilds רבי ישמעאל's argument: if a bull and a goat have matched actions, then two bulls should surely be matched.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: in a case where the offerings are not alike, since one is a bull and one is a goat, the actions are still matched according to what is written about them. So in a case where the offerings are alike, since both are bulls, isn't it logical...
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the pair has been identified, the גמרא spells out how רבי ישמעאל's קל וחומר works. The sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'lighter' case is a bull and a goat: different animals whose blood actions are still matched. The 'heavier' case is the bull of יום הכפורים and the bull of the כהן משיח, which are the same animal. If the matching applies in the lighter case, it surely applies in the heavier one, so no extra word in the פסוק is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what he is saying (an explanation of someone's words)
Were made equal or matched
Actions, here the blood procedures
Isn't it logical? (the closing of a קל וחומר)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why רבי ישמעאל, unlike רבי, does not need the word ״לַפָּר״ to link the two bulls.

phrases.english: And this is what he is saying: Just as in a case
where offering was not matched with offering
since this is a bull and that is a goat
the actions were still matched with the actions
for what is written about them
then in a case where offering is matched with offering
since this is a bull and that is a bull
phrases.notes: These are the bull of יום הכפורים and the bull of the כהן משיח.

phrases.english: isn't it logical...

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכִי קָאָמַר: וּמָה בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁלֹּא הוּשְׁווּ קׇרְבָּן לְקׇרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the pair identified in step 12 to rebuild the קל וחומר from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since a bull and a goat have matched blood actions, two bulls surely have matched blood actions.
